provenance.statementCoordinateFile: This item was created from a cadastral coordinate file (.txt) — the Stereo 70 corner coordinates were read from the file and used to build the geometry.
provenance.statementAlgorithm: This item was generated automatically by an algorithm (e.g. polygon division or geometric computation).
provenance.statementAiInterpreted: This item was interpreted by an AI model from an image or document via a cloud API — the result should be reviewed by a person.

STR-01.requirement: The folder you choose contains only folders: one per property, plus comune and flotante if you need them. No file sits directly in it.

STR-04.requirement: Every folder in the chosen folder is either a property, or comune, or flotante. A property name carries the tarla, a hyphen, then the parcela — and, if you want one, a second hyphen and a free description. per stands in for the slash, which cannot be used in a folder name.

STR-05.requirement: The shared folders are named exactly comune and flotante, in lower case.

DUP-01.requirement: The same file must not sit in the chosen folder more than once. The system recognises copies by name and by size, looking past the ending Windows adds when you copy a file, such as “ - Copy”. Files whose name is nothing but a number are treated as scanned pages and are not compared with each other: a page cannot be taken out of a document without breaking its numbering. Documents scanned into page folders are compared whole, under the next rule; pages left directly in the property's folder are not checked at all.
DUP-01.example: Wrong: “contract vanzare.pdf” and “contract vanzare - Copy.pdf” both sit in the property's folder. Right: the file sits in one place only, and the copy has been taken out of the chosen folder.
DUP-01.violation: {sets, plural, one {One file sits in the chosen folder more than once} other {# files sit in the chosen folder more than once}}, {files, plural, one {one file} other {# files}} in total. Look at each group below: if they really are the same file, keep the one in the right place and take the others out of the chosen folder. If they are different documents, rename one of them so they no longer look alike. If you cannot tell, take them all out of the chosen folder — you can import them later.

DUP-02.requirement: The same document must not sit in more than one page folder inside the chosen folder. The system compares the pages: two folders holding exactly the same pages are very probably one and the same document, copied — even when the folders are named differently. Where the pages alone are not enough — a folder with a single page, or several pages of one size — the folders are only reported when one of them is marked as a copy and sits beside the other.
DUP-02.example: Wrong: “Contract vanzare” and “Contract vanzare - Copy” hold the same scanned pages. Right: the document sits in one page folder only, and the copy has been taken out of the chosen folder.
DUP-02.violation: {sets, plural, one {One document sits in more than one page folder} other {# documents sit in more than one page folder}}, {folders, plural, one {one folder} other {# folders}} in total. Open the folders below and compare the pages: if they are the same, keep one folder and take the others out of the chosen folder. If they are different documents, rename one of the folders so they no longer look alike. If you cannot tell, take them all out of the chosen folder — you can import them later.

PEX-01.explanation: A document in the chosen folder counts as already in the system when the archive holds a document with exactly the same files — the same file names and the same sizes — brought into the system under the same name: the file's name or the page folder's name. For a page folder every page is compared, not just the first. If you have since renamed the files or the page folder, or renumbered the pages, the system no longer recognises it and will import it again. Until now, renaming the document in the system also forced a new import: for documents the import brings in from this version onwards it no longer has that effect, and for those that entered the archive before this version the comparison uses the title they carry now — so if the AI read changed it after import, the document will be imported again.
PEX-01.example: Right: “Contract vanzare.pdf” in the property's folder is 240 KB, and the archive already holds a document that came from the file “Contract vanzare.pdf” with a single 240 KB file — it is the same document and is not imported a second time. For documents the import brings in from this version onwards, this still holds when the document now has a different title in the archive: for those, the comparison is not made against the archived title but against the name they were brought in under. Where the archived document has a title, it is printed on its row so you can see which document it is. Otherwise: if the file in the folder has a different name or a different size, it is treated as a new document.

PEX-02.explanation: A document that is already in the system is not imported a second time. If the file sits in a property folder in this import, the archived document is linked to that property instead, so you will find the property with the document attached and no second copy anywhere. If the file belongs to no property in this import, nothing happens to it at all.
PEX-02.example: A land-registry extract imported last year now sits in the folder for property 48-50: no second document is created, and the extract that already exists is linked to property 48-50.

PEX-03.explanation: Identity cards are imported again even when they appear to be here already. The reason is deliberate: the one in the system may have expired, and two copies of the same person are less serious than a person missing altogether. The system recognises an identity card by its file name, so make a note of these files and check the people after the import has finished.
PEX-03.example: “Buletin Ionescu.jpg” appears to be here already, but it is imported anyway. After the import, open the person Ionescu and see whether the details are the ones on the new card.

PEX-04.explanation: Coordinate files are imported again even when they appear to be here already. A property's corners have to show which document they were read from, and that document is created by this import — had the file been skipped, the new property would be left with corners and no source.
PEX-04.example: “coord 48-50.txt” has been imported once before, but it is imported again because the corners of property 48-50 in this import are made from it.

cardsBlocked.whatNext: Open the folder in File Explorer and split each file above so that there is one file per identity card — one person, one file. Leave them where they are and give them names that say whose card each one is. ⚠ If the file sits inside a page folder — one whose files are numbered 1, 2, 3… — do not split it in there: the files in such a folder are the pages of ONE document, so two identity cards left inside it would still become one document and the second person would never be created at all. Take the page out of the page folder and put each identity card beside that folder as a file of its own. The pages left inside do not need renumbering — it is always the first page that comes out, and the run may start at any number. If the page folder is left empty, delete it: an empty folder stops the next run. Then start the import again: every check before the classification costs nothing.
cardsBlocked.noWaiver: There is no “continue anyway” here, unlike the screen that asks for forms. A document type without a form is a call you are entitled to make; a scan holding two people's identity cards is not. It would put into the archive one document carrying two people's papers, and where the file sits inside a property folder it would also produce a person carrying one person's name and another's CNP — a person who does not exist and whom nothing would ever flag.

information.title: How the import works
information.lead: The import runs in steps — the ones above. At each step the system checks one thing and shows you exactly what it found.
information.stops: Several times it will stop and ask you to put something right in the folder on your computer: rename a folder, move a file, or delete a spare copy. When that happens, open the folder in File Explorer, make the change, then come back here and press the re-check button. This is not a fault — it is how the import is meant to work.
information.neverTouchesFiles: The system never touches your files. It does not move them, rename them or delete them. You are the only one who changes them, from File Explorer.
information.nothingSavedUntilTheEnd: Nothing goes into the archive until the Import step. Until then you can cancel at any time, and before it cancels you are told exactly what is left behind.

infoPanel.title: Ce este o Ștampilă?
infoPanel.body1: O ștampilă definește o caracteristică pe termen lung sau permanentă a obiectelor — persoane, proprietăți sau documente, indiferent de tip. De exemplu, o inițiativă de doi ani care implică multe persoane, proprietăți și documente primește o ștampilă specifică.
infoPanel.body2: Spre deosebire de grupuri, o ștampilă poate fi aplicată simultan pe orice combinație de tipuri de entități.
infoPanel.body3: Ștampilele pot descrie și calificatori subiectivi: nivelul de încredere ATT, potențialul unui obiect, prioritatea sau orice altă etichetă de evaluare personală. Este o practică recomandată să aplici cât mai multe ștampile și să creezi ștampile variate — aceasta adaugă valoare și bogăție utilizării datelor.
infoPanel.codeNote: Fiecare ștampilă primește un cod unic de trei litere (ex. STMP-AAA) atribuit automat.
infoPanel.seeAlso: Pentru acțiuni temporare pe un singur tip de obiect, folosește Grupuri.

infoPanel.title: Ce este un Grup?
infoPanel.body1: Un grup reunește elemente de un singur tip — proprietăți, persoane fizice, persoane juridice sau documente — pentru acțiuni și activități pe termen scurt. De exemplu: grupezi câteva proprietăți pentru o evaluare, câteva persoane pentru a le trimite un mesaj, sau câteva documente relevante pentru un eveniment cu o instituție.
infoPanel.body2: Elementele pot face parte din unul sau mai multe grupuri și pot fi eliminate oricând. Când un grup și-a îndeplinit misiunea, poate fi șters — elementele continuă să există independent.
infoPanel.codeNote: Fiecare grup primește un cod numeric unic (ex. GRP-001, GRP-002…) atribuit automat.
infoPanel.seeAlso: Pentru caracteristici pe termen lung sau permanente care se aplică pe mai multe tipuri de obiecte, folosește Ștampile.
